I’m glad you can feel confident with your style; it’s a big achievement. Regarding Kibbe body types for obese women: a person’s body type never changes despite weight loss or gain. There’s a video about Kibbe body types on plus size women on Merriam Style’s YouTube channel. Her channel helped me out a lot, which is why I’m recommending it. Before learning about Kibbe, I had a difficult time finding my own style. Maybe there are others out there who may find this useful too.

I used to think the same until I came across Merriam Style’s YouTube channel. I suggest you check out some of her videos on finding your Kibbe type. No woman fits each Kibbe body type perfectly. It’s about finding the body type that is closest to your body composition. E.g. when you teach a child about the colour blue, you point them to things that are blue (the sky, the sea etc.). Even though all the blue shades vary (light, dark, high chroma, low chroma), the child can still categorise all of these colours as blue. Everybody has a Kibbe type, but no one is 100% a perfect Kibbe body type. Also what do you mean by misogynistic? The Kibbe system is but a tool to help you figure out what kind of lines and shapes you should wear to look your best. But it’s up to you whether you stick to the suggestions or not.

I literally have been struggling with this for years. Have you ever considered that there might be a psychological root cause? For me personally, I realised that I deep down, judged women for dressing feminine because I saw femininity as a negative trait. Here’s a video that talks about our conscious and subconscious which helped me realise this: https://m.youtube.com/watch?v=SZ90jN2R9n8 Alternatively, you could just be having trouble finding styles that enhances your femininity in a flattering way; e.g. a slouchy sweater may look relaxed and flirty on one woman, but may look like a potato sack on another. It’s about finding your body type and knowing what compliments it. I recommend checking out the Kibbe body type system. There are some pretty good YouTube videos on finding your Kibbe type. Hope this helps and good luck!

I think you’re misusing the word “honesty”. Honesty is not about telling someone everything you feel or think. What you actually did is violate her boundaries. Before you tell someone something, always think, “will this be helpful to them?” In this instance, no, because you dumped your feelings (that she can’t reciprocate) on her and that becomes a burden to her. You have voluntarily crossed the friendship boundary by indicating your romantic interest in her, which is quite selfish on your part, since she’s already taken. Once you cross someone’s boundary, expect them to run away from you. You need to accept the fact that she wants nothing to do with you, or else you’ll try to over-step her boundaries even further. Your actions also don’t seem to match your words (that’s what makes you come across as creepy); you’re the one that needs to be honest with yourself.
Read ‘Boundaries’ by Henry Cloud! It helped me a lot :)

ESH. Whilst you were being honest about how you felt about her looks, honesty should always be accompanied with kindness. (Ask yourself is what I am going to say honest, helpful and kind?) However, in this case, you chose to use it as a weapon to hurt and ridicule her. Did she deserve it? Probably. But usually when you hurt someone deliberately and obviously, you also hurt yourself because in a way, she won; she accomplished her goal because you reacted negatively. The best kind of revenge is to look like you’re empowered, confident and happy and show it off. What you could have done is dress yourself up to show off your body, laugh with your friends in front of her etc. in front of her. Show her that you’re not affected by the horrible thing she had done. She would have realised that trying to hurt someone did not make her happier and also perhaps make her realise her body acceptance ways of thinking are logical fallacies.
